newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slide on falling dollar worries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slide on falling dollar worries.

text.p: Argentine bonds were lower late morning Friday in nervous activity after U.S. Treasuries fell in the wake of a dollar slide against the mark.
"Everybody is looking at the dollar to mark rate," said a trader at a foreign bank.

With the dollar falling against the mark on concerns that the Bundesbank, Germany's central bank, could raise rates next week, investors took profits by selling U.S. assets. The recent climb of the dollar against the mark has made the profits of U.S. assets for foreign investors that much larger.
Argentina's Par Brady bond fell 3/8 to 74 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 fell $0.70 to 119.20.
Another trader said there was some heavy selling of the Par bond early on, but volume declined sharply through the morning as investors decided to stay on the sidelines until calm returns.
"Now there is not much happening," said the trader.
